chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'For every prayer there are two times, and the first of the two times is its best; and no one may make the last of the two times the time [for prayer] except for an excuse that is not due to a valid reason [i.e., negligence].'
ai.seo_question: What are the two times for each prayer in Shia jurisprudence and when is it permissible to delay?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the temporal boundaries of obligatory prayers, emphasizing that the initial period (awwal al-waqt) holds superior merit and is the default state for believers. This narration underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'ibtida' al-waqt' (commencement of time) while cautioning against 'ta'khir' (delay) without a valid excuse ('udhr), thereby distinguishing between permissible deferral and negligent procrastination. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the hierarchy of prayer times in fiqh al-Sadiq.
